title: WP Admin Shell — App Manifest (v1)
description: Declares what an admin shell app is. Shipped alongside the app's code (script and style assets), discovered at the convention path `{plugin}/apps/{name}/app.json` or registered programmatically. The manifest contains only intrinsic, install-independent declarations: the app's ARIA role, the platform services it requests from its hosting engine, the WordPress capabilities required to mount it, and the configuration schema it accepts when admin.json passes values. Manifests deliberately do not declare layout, geometry, keystroke bindings, or which install they belong to — those are install decisions and live in admin.json. See WP Admin Shell Design Spec §4.1.

$schema.description: Reference to this schema document. Conventionally `https://schemas.wp.org/admin-app/v1.json`. Optional but strongly recommended — IDE tooling uses it for live validation. Relative paths are accepted (e.g., `../docs/schemas/admin-app-v2.json` for in-repo authoring), matching the block.json convention.

id.description: Globally unique app identifier. Format: `{namespace}:{name}`. The `core` namespace is reserved for apps shipped with the WP Admin Shell plugin; the `plugin` namespace requires `plugin:{slug}/{name}` where `slug` matches the contributing plugin's directory name. Names within a namespace are kebab-case. Examples: `core:command-palette`, `core:posts`, `plugin:woocommerce/orders`. The runtime registry rejects duplicate ids; plugins extending core apps must use a different id and have admin.json route to their version.

version.description: Manifest schema version this document conforms to. v1 is the current shape. Bump only on breaking changes to this app's manifest contract (e.g., field renames, type changes). Adding optional fields does not require a version bump. The runtime accepts higher versions with a warning and best-effort load: known fields are honored, unknown fields preserved on the manifest object but ignored.

title.description: Human-readable name of the app, shown in command palettes, navigation menus, error messages, and developer tooling. Translatable. Should be short — typically two or three words.

description.description: Optional human-readable description of what the app does. Used in admin.json authoring tools, plugin install screens, and ecosystem directories. Translatable. One sentence to a short paragraph.

designSystem.description: Design system the app's render tree emits components from. Free-form string by convention: `@wordpress/ui` (WPDS, the WordPress Design System — used by every `core:*` app), `mui` (Material Design), `chakra`, `radix`, `custom`, etc. Apps are bound to their design system because they import its component primitives directly; mounting a `@wordpress/ui` app inside a Material engine produces visually inconsistent results. The kernel emits a dev-mode warning when the active engine's declared `designSystem` differs from a mounted app's. Optional — apps that don't declare a value are treated as DS-unknown and skip the mismatch check.

role.description: The app's primary ARIA role when mounted into a region. Drives engine specialization: engines that recognize the role apply specialized chrome (e.g., a `navigation` app gets sidebar treatment in the wp-default engine). Roles outside an engine's specializes-roles list fall through to the engine's default arrangement. Required because every mounted app must have a defined accessibility role for screen readers. Common values: `main`, `dialog`, `navigation`, `complementary`, `banner`, `contentinfo`, `region`, `search`. Any valid WAI-ARIA 1.2 role is accepted.

platform.description: Platform service requests. The app declares which engine-provided services it needs — modality, focus management, dismissal handling, dirty-state tracking, keyboard triggerability. Each field maps to a service the browser/OS would provide if this were a website running in a browser. Engines declare in their own manifest which services they implement; an app requesting a service the active engine does not honor still mounts, but the unhonored request is a no-op (with a logged warning in development). See spec §5.3.

capabilities.description: WordPress capabilities required to mount this app. The user must have all listed capabilities; missing any one suppresses the app. This is the floor for any consumer — admin.json cannot lower this requirement, only add to it. Capabilities are validated against `core-data`'s `canUser()` for entity caps and a custom REST endpoint for non-entity caps. Empty array means no capability is required (rare; even the command palette typically requires `read`). Examples: `["edit_posts"]`, `["manage_options", "upload_files"]`.

config-schema.description: JSON Schema document describing the shape of the `config` object that admin.json passes to this app at mount time (either via a region's `config` field or via a routes entry's `config` field). The runtime validates the merged config against this schema before mounting; validation failure prevents mount and surfaces an authoring error. The schema is itself a JSON Schema document; recursive validation against the JSON Schema meta-schema is not enforced by the runtime but is recommended via author tooling.

extension-points.description: Documentary listing of slot/fill, filter hooks, and other React or PHP extension surfaces this app exposes to plugins. Not load-bearing: the runtime does not read or enforce this field. Included for IDE tooling, ecosystem documentation, and machine-readable discovery of app extensibility surfaces. Keys are extension-point identifiers (e.g., `PluginSidebar`, `PluginDocumentSettingPanel`); values are the WordPress package or hook namespace where the extension is registered (e.g., `@wordpress/editor`).

^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$.description: Package or hook namespace where consumers register extensions for this point.

script.description: WordPress script handle for this app's JavaScript bundle. Must already be registered with WordPress (via `wp_register_script`) before the manifest references it. The runtime enqueues this handle when the app mounts, supporting WordPress's standard dependency resolution and code-splitting. Same pattern as `block.json`'s `editorScript`.

style.description: Optional WordPress style handle for this app's CSS. Enqueued alongside the script when the app mounts. Apps with no dedicated styles (relying entirely on WPDS tokens for theming) may omit this field.

viewConfig.description: Optional primary view-config the app ships as its baseline. Names the entity `(kind, name[, variant])` this app renders. The runtime merges this baseline with admin.json `viewConfigs` overrides and filter-driven overrides; the consuming app reads the resolved value via `useViewConfig`. Apps that don't render a single entity (command palette, dashboard) omit this field. See spec §13 #7.

allOf.description: Conditional rule: `platform.block-navigation-on-dirty` is meaningful only if `platform.dirty-state` is also true. Apps that don't track dirty state cannot block navigation on it.

ariaRole.description: A WAI-ARIA 1.2 role name. Lowercase, alphabetic. The runtime does not enforce a closed list — any valid ARIA role is accepted — but engines specialize for a subset (typically the landmark roles plus `dialog`). Common values for shell apps: `main` (primary content), `dialog` (modal/non-modal dialogs), `navigation` (nav menus), `complementary` (side panels and inspectors), `banner` (top-of-page header), `contentinfo` (footer/status info), `search` (search interfaces), `region` (generic landmark). Avoid widget roles (`button`, `checkbox`, etc.) — those describe controls, not regions or apps. See https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#role_definitions.

wpCapability.description: A WordPress capability name. Lowercase, alphanumeric and underscore, matching WordPress's capability naming conventions. Standard capabilities include `read`, `edit_posts`, `manage_options`, `upload_files`, `list_users`, `manage_woocommerce`, etc. Custom capabilities registered by plugins follow the same pattern.

appPlatform.description: Platform services this app requests from its hosting engine. Each field corresponds to a service with a clear browser/OS analog — services every region author would otherwise reimplement identically. The list is governed centrally and grows additively in minor spec versions; engines opt into honoring each service via their own `honored-platform` array.

core:modal.description: When true, the app should be rendered with focus trapped inside its region, ARIA modal attributes applied, and (for engines that support it) a backdrop scrim rendered behind the region. Browser analog: HTML `<dialog>` with `showModal()`. Use for command palettes, confirmation dialogs, full-screen takeover apps. Implies that other regions cannot receive interaction while the app is mounted.

items.description: A trigger that dismisses (unmounts) this app's region. `Escape` = pressing Escape key; `backdrop-click` = clicking outside the region while a modal backdrop is shown; `outside-click` = clicking outside the region without a backdrop (e.g., for non-modal popovers); `navigation` = any URL navigation event.

core:dismiss-on.description: Triggers that cause the engine to unmount this app's region. Browser analog: HTML `<dialog>` Escape-to-close behavior, popover dismissal. Use for ephemeral apps (modals, palettes, drawers). Apps mounted in persistent regions typically omit this field — they live for the life of the shell. Multiple triggers are honored simultaneously.

core:autofocus-target.description: CSS selector identifying which element should receive focus when this app mounts. Browser analog: HTML `autofocus` attribute. The selector is evaluated against the app's rendered DOM after mount. If the selector matches no element (or matches multiple — first wins), focus falls through to the engine's default — typically the region's container element. Use for apps where a specific input or button should receive focus immediately (search fields in a command palette, the title input in a new-post editor).

core:triggerable.description: When true, this app can be invoked by a binding declared in admin.json's `bindings` block (e.g., `Mod+K` opens the command palette). Browser analog: HTML `commandfor` / `command` attributes. The app declares only that it accepts being invoked; the actual keystroke or invocation source is decided at install time in admin.json. Apps that should never be invoked by user shortcut (e.g., always-mounted persistent system apps) omit this field. Note: setting this to `true` does not register a binding — admin.json must explicitly bind a keystroke to the app's id.

core:persists-across-navigation.description: When true, this app's region survives URL-driven changes to other regions. Browser analog: persistent browser tabs (a tab's content survives when other tabs navigate). Use for navigation sidebars, status bars, and other UI that should remain mounted across content changes. Apps in routable regions (regions with `routing.route-key`) typically omit this field — they unmount when the URL slot they read from changes.

core:dirty-state.description: When true, this app may report unsaved-changes state via the runtime's dirty-state API. Engines honoring this field will query the app before unmounting and may delay or prevent navigation if state is dirty. Browser analog: `beforeunload` event. Use for editor-style apps where unsaved changes matter. Apps without unsaved-state semantics (read-only views, simple displays) omit this field. Setting this true is a prerequisite for `block-navigation-on-dirty`.

core:block-navigation-on-dirty.description: When true (and `dirty-state` is also true), the engine shows a confirmation dialog before unmounting the app while it reports dirty state. Browser analog: the `beforeunload` confirmation dialog. Use for editors where data loss must be guarded against. Without this field, dirty state is reported but does not block navigation — the app is responsible for any other warning UX. Setting this without also setting `dirty-state: true` is a manifest error and rejected by the schema.

windowSize.description: A `{ w, h }` pixel pair used by windowing engines for default + minimum window dimensions. Pixels, not tokens — these are author-supplied hints describing the app's preferred viewport. Engines that don't host windowed mounts ignore the value.

appWindow.description: Optional window-mount hints for engines that mount this app inside a window-frame region (windowed/MDI/desktop-style engines). Default engines (sidebar+toolbar+content) ignore the block entirely. Added 2026-05-12 alongside the `core:dynamic-children` platform service (spec §5.5). The block is purely declarative: engines consult it on mount and apply sensible defaults if any field is missing.

defaultSize.description: Preferred initial window size in CSS pixels. Authors pick values that frame the app's first view at a comfortable density — e.g., a posts list at 960×720, a settings page at 720×600. Engines may override based on viewport size.

minSize.description: Minimum window size in CSS pixels. The compositor enforces this floor when the user resizes — content below this size becomes unusable. Defaults to engine policy (typically 320×240) when omitted.

chrome.description: Engine-defined window chrome style identifier. Engines that ship multiple frame styles (e.g., `default`, `minimal`, `dialog`) accept the matching id here. Unrecognized values fall back to the engine's default chrome. Acts as a documentation hint — the engine is the source of truth for valid values.

multiInstance.description: When true, the app may be opened as multiple simultaneous windows with independent state (e.g., two posts lists with different post-type configs side-by-side). When false (default), opening a second window of this app focuses the existing one. Apps with singleton semantics — settings pages, site-wide tool panels — omit this field. Engines that don't differentiate single-vs-multi instance ignore the value.

icon.description: Icon registry name (resolved by the active engine's icon table via the kernel icon registry). Used by windowing engines for the window-frame titlebar icon, taskbar/dock entry, and overview switcher. Defaults to a generic application icon when omitted.

appDocumentation.description: Documentation contract: machine-readable description of what the app does at runtime, intended for reviewers, ecosystem tooling, and authors rebuilding the app on a different design system or framework. Not load-bearing: the runtime does not read or enforce any field here. The contract pairs with a sibling `app.md` prose document — structured facts live here, narrative explanation lives in markdown.

purpose.description: Extended one-paragraph plain-English description of what the app does, who it serves, and how it fits into the shell. Longer-form than the manifest `description` field (which is a one-line summary used in plugin install screens). Translatable.

rebuilds.description: Reference to a tier-2 screen specification under `docs/screens/` that this app rebuilds, expressed as the screen slug (e.g. `dashboard-home`, `posts`, `users`). Omitted for apps with no wp-admin screen equivalent (shell-only apps like `core:navigation`, `core:site-hub`).

data.description: Data dependencies the app expresses against the WordPress runtime. Reads and writes are listed separately so a reimplementation can wire up the read path before the write path. The list should cover every entity, REST endpoint, or window global the app touches in production — not implementation-internal helpers.

reads.description: Data sources the app reads from. Each entry names a source, the access mechanism, and (if applicable) the WordPress REST context and notable query args.

writes.description: Data mutations the app performs. Each entry names a source, an operation kind, and any cache-invalidation responsibilities a reimplementation must mirror.

url.description: URL participation contract. Per spec §6 / §18, the URL is the canonical state store for routable regions and any cross-region coordination. An app declares which URL slots it reads from, which it writes back, and which route patterns it navigates to.

reads-slots.description: Named URL query slots the app reads. Use `_self` for the primary hash path; use the slot name otherwise (e.g. `screen`, `detail`).

writes-slots.description: Named URL query slots the app writes through the router (e.g. NavigationApp writes `screen` for drill-down state).

navigates.description: Route patterns the app navigates to via `navigate()` or anchor hrefs. Patterns use `{param}` placeholders (e.g. `#/posts/{id}/edit`, `#/media`). Listing them here documents the outbound link surface.

states.description: User-visible runtime states the app cycles through. Lists the discriminated states a reimplementation must render; intermediate / transient states (debounce ticks, hover) are out of scope.

when.description: Condition that puts the app into this state (e.g. `records === null`, `hasEdits && isSaving`).

renders.description: What the user sees in this state — short prose. Reimplementations target this output, not the specific component.

interactions.description: User actions the app responds to. Each entry is a trigger → effect pair; nested triggers (a modal that opens another modal) are flattened into separate entries.

trigger.description: User input or system event (e.g. `Click row title`, `Press Cmd+S`, `Submit Quick Draft form`, `Drag avatar onto upload zone`).

effect.description: State change, navigation, or mutation that results (e.g. `Navigate to #/posts/{id}/edit`, `POST /wp/v2/posts and invalidate the drafts query`).

guards.description: Capability checks, eligibility checks, or invariants enforced before the effect runs (e.g. `userCan("edit_post", item)`, `status === "publish"`).

a11y.description: Accessibility contract a reimplementation must preserve. Landmark role is already declared in the top-level `role` field; this block covers focus, keyboard, and screen-reader concerns that aren't otherwise discoverable.

focus-management.description: How the app manages focus on mount, route changes, modal open/close, and post-action transitions.

keyboard.description: App-owned keyboard shortcuts. Shell-level bindings (the `bindings` block in admin.json) are out of scope.

keys.description: Display name of the keystroke chord (e.g. `Cmd+S`, `Esc`, `Enter`).

screen-reader.description: Live regions, `aria-live` announcements, `aria-current` usage, and other screen-reader-specific affordances.

constraints.description: Framework-, WPDS-, or WordPress-specific gotchas a reimplementation must account for. Captures the recurring patterns documented in `CLAUDE.md` (null-guards, cache invalidation, DataViews import path) and any per-app workarounds.

note.description: What the constraint is and what a reimplementation must do to honor it.

design-system-leakage.description: Specific `@wordpress/*` imports the app cannot do without. A rebuild on a non-WPDS design system (Material, Tailwind, custom) must provide functional equivalents for every entry. In scope: any package whose API shape a non-WPDS rebuild needs a substitute for, including UI components (`@wordpress/ui`, `@wordpress/components`, `@wordpress/dataviews`), data-binding packages (`@wordpress/core-data`, `@wordpress/api-fetch`, `@wordpress/notices`, `@wordpress/commands`), block-editor packages (`@wordpress/block-editor`, `@wordpress/blocks`), and DS-adjacent helpers (`@wordpress/icons`, `@wordpress/html-entities`, `@wordpress/url`, `@wordpress/keycodes`). Out of scope: framework primitives (`@wordpress/element`, `@wordpress/i18n`, `@wordpress/data`) and intra-app imports (relative paths between bundled apps).

purpose.description: What the import provides and why the app needs it.

dataOperation.description: A single data-read operation: which source the app pulls from, by what mechanism, and what shape the data has.

source.description: REST endpoint (e.g. `/wp/v2/posts`), `core-data` entity path (e.g. `postType/post`, `root/site`, `root/user`), external URL, or window-global property (e.g. `window.wpAdminShell.user`).

via.description: Access mechanism. `core-data` = `useEntityRecord`/`useEntityRecords` from `@wordpress/core-data`; `api-fetch` = `@wordpress/api-fetch` direct call (includes apps that read a sync cache populated by an `api-fetch` REST call, e.g. the `userCan` helper); `window-global` = read from `window.wpAdminShell.*` (config injected by PHP); `external` = `fetch()` against a non-WordPress origin; `commands` = `@wordpress/commands` registry; `kernel-config` = props passed by the runtime from the resolved admin.json tree or kernel context (e.g. `config.styles.branding`, `config.routes`, `config.left/right`).

context.description: REST context, when applicable. `edit` is required for any field whose `raw` value will be edited (title, content, excerpt). Omit for non-REST sources.

purpose.description: What this read is for in the app's flow (e.g. `List rows in the DataViews table`, `Look up the acting user for self-delete guard`).

fields.description: Notable fields read from the record (e.g. `["title.raw", "status", "author", "date"]`). Use dotted paths for nested values.

query.description: Notable query args the app passes (e.g. `{ _embed: "author", per_page: 20 }`). Dynamic args (search strings, filter values) document the keys, not the values.

appViewConfig.description: An app-shipped view-config baseline. Same shape as the top-level admin.json `viewConfigs` entry, with required `kind`/`name` and optional `variant` so the entity binding is self-describing. Cascade-overrideable: admin.json `viewConfigs[kind][name|variant]` wins per-field; filter `wp_admin_shell_view_config_{kind}_{name}[_{variant}]` runs last.

kind.description: Entity kind, matching `@wordpress/core-data` entity kinds (`postType`, `root`, `taxonomy`, etc.).

variant.description: Optional variant identifier. Forward-slash namespacing allowed (e.g. `woocommerce-bookings/services`). Omitted = base view-config.

fieldsRef.description: Reference to a `fieldCollections` entry id. See admin-v2 `viewConfigEntry.fieldsRef`.

dataMutation.description: A single data-write operation: which source the app mutates, by what mechanism, and what cache invalidations are required afterwards.

source.description: REST endpoint or `core-data` entity path (same shape as `dataOperation.source`).

via.description: Mutation mechanism. `core-data` = `saveEntityRecord` / `deleteEntityRecord` via `useDispatch(coreStore)`; `api-fetch` = direct call; `external` = non-WordPress origin.

operation.description: Operation kind. `partial-update` = PATCH with a subset of fields (used for comment moderation status changes); `trash` = the WordPress default delete that sends to trash (no `force` flag); `delete` = permanent delete (`force: true`).

purpose.description: What this write is for (e.g. `Approve a pending comment`, `Trash one or more selected posts`).

invalidates.description: Cache keys or entity queries that must be invalidated afterwards. `core-data`'s `useEntityRecord` short-circuits for the same store, but `useEntityRecords` queries do not — explicit `invalidateResolution( 'getEntityRecords', [...] )` calls are required. List the entity paths the reimplementation must invalidate (e.g. `postType/post`).
